record_identity.title: DNB employees faced live deepfake impersonation of bank executives in attempted transfer fraud

incident_identity.historical_event_name: DNB live executive deepfake fraud attempt
incident_identity.date_basis: BankShift reports the suspicious WhatsApp approach on 21 January 2025 and the observed Teams meeting on 23 January; the DNB retrospective places the CEO-fraud attempt in January.

summary: On 21 January 2025, managers at DNB’s Singapore office received WhatsApp messages appearing to come from CFO Ida Lerner, inviting them to a meeting with her and CEO Kjerstin Braathen about a new product; similar messages reached other international managers. A Singapore manager reported the suspicious invitation to DNB security under the bank’s procedures. Security identified fraud indicators and chose to observe the Microsoft Teams meeting on 23 January. The meeting showed purported versions of Braathen and Lerner with familiar voices and appearances. The purported Lerner presented an investment opportunity and asked staff to transfer several million Singapore dollars. DNB ended contact when payment instructions appeared, and reported no financial loss. DNB later described the executive audio and video as AI/deepfake manipulation; its review found that existing online recordings had been used and looped.

vigil_assessment.factual_basis: BankShift’s original report quotes DNB’s then chief executive and security director and dates the suspicious WhatsApp approach to 21 January and the Teams meeting to 23 January 2025. The Singapore manager reported the invitation through an existing security procedure before the meeting; the security team identified CEO-fraud signs and deliberately allowed the call to proceed to observe the method. In the meeting, a purported CFO requested a transfer of several million Singapore dollars as an investment opportunity. The security director said DNB broke contact when payment instructions were displayed. He described recognisable voices, image and accent, some connection breaks, and source recordings available online that appeared to have been looped. DNB’s 2026 threat report independently confirms AI/deepfake manipulation of executive audio and video in the January attempted CEO fraud. AIID also reports that DNB avoided loss. The public evidence establishes attempted solicitation and timely security intervention, not a completed transfer, a particular generator or model, a proven unauthorised synthesis-control decision, the attacker’s identity, or the complete payment-control trace. The freshly accessible DNB report distinguishes adapted CEO footage, manipulated CFO voice and silent looped purported external participants. It corroborates the attempt while leaving the generation service and private transaction controls unspecified.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: The fraudsters concealed AI manipulation in a purported executive meeting. DNB’s staff escalation and after-action review are documented, and no transfer loss is reported. Complete AI-specific risk and response arrangements remain unresolved. Ending contact is not treated as deactivation of the generation system.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: Familiar video, voice and senior title can supply false transaction authority even in an apparently live meeting. Here the manager’s reporting route, security review and intervention held under that pressure; those distinct protective stages matter as much to governance analysis as the attempted deception.
assessment_boundaries: The original report relies on DNB personnel statements; the underlying meeting recording and investigation file were not independently examined here.
DNB describes AI/deepfake manipulation and looped online source recordings; the exact model, real-time generation method, requester identity and generator-side authority state are not public.
The security procedure and response are evidenced, but specific payment-approval controls and their activation states are not described.
The attempt was interrupted before a reported transfer. The requested amount is not materialised financial loss.

dimensions.assessment_basis: No injury, illness or medical safety consequence is reported in the attempted executive-payment fraud. There was no direct physical safety test from which zero injury could be certified.
The convincing impersonation and security investigation do not establish distress, suffering or an adverse psychological consequence to an employee or executive.

Public executive footage was reused and a voice manipulated. The available sources do not establish compromised private data, unauthorised access to an employee account or a bandable confidentiality consequence.

AIID expressly reports avoided loss. DNB’s originating report confirms pre-meeting fraud identification and deliberate observation; BankShift reports cutoff at payment instructions. Together these support bounded financial S1 with medium confidence. Requested millions are not realised loss. No exact numeric loss or currency conversion is invented.
